title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI
slides: Ramp hits $60B—what does it mean for spend management?
Its AI now audits expenses autonomously
But it also replaces human finance teams
Your CFO must decide: integrate or resist?
Test Ramp's AI on one expense report today
thread_text:
1. $60B wake-up call

A company just hit a $60B valuation by letting AI approve expense reports. The same machine that replaces your approval workflow now decides what gets reimbursed.

2. Autopilot for expenses

Ramp's AI audits receipts and flags anomalies without a human. It learns patterns, catches duplicates, and auto-approves low-risk claims in seconds.

3. CFOs face a choice

Integrating AI means fewer finance hires, faster closes, and less manual review. Resisting means staying competitive but slower—and your team knows it.

4. The human cost

One finance team replaced three full-time reviewers with a single AI config. The CFO now approves exceptions only—not every line item. That shift is permanent.

5. Test it today

Take one real expense report and ask ChatGPT to audit it for duplicates or missing receipts. If it catches even one error, your CFO needs to see that this week.
